messages:
sam: Heads-up: did a quick throughput vs tail scan on model-class-C with varied microbatch targets and a new 'latency budget gate' for prefill. p95 drifted when microbatch >7. Collected prefill/decode percentiles, kernel switch counts, kv admission logs. My rough idea: treat prefill as a soft budget (max 40% of SLO) and force kv admission stricter when prefill budget exceeded. Also try microbatch_target=6 for C. Thoughts?

perf-bot: perf snapshot (canary pool): model=C seq=768
- mb=8 baseline: p50=62ms p95=310ms p99=620ms
- mb=6 + kv_gate: p50=65ms p95=255ms p99=540ms
- decode kernel fallbacks +18% during 1-2s spikes
link: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/runtime/prefill-decode/2166667777

jess: Can you paste the prefill/decode breakdown by percentile? want to see which stage moves.

sam: sure: 
```
prefill (mb=8): p50=78ms p95=120ms p99=200ms
decode  (mb=8): p50= -  p95=190ms p99=420ms
prefill (mb=6): p95=110ms p99=180ms
decode  (mb=6): p95=145ms p99=360ms
```
Most win shows up on decode tail — microbatch reduction reduces queuing on decode kernels and cuts kernel selection churn. Prefill also edges down slightly.

ian: What exactly is your kv admission gate? last time we tightened it we saw cache warmup regress for low-traffic tenants.

sam: implemented simple gate: admit_kv = (kv_hit_rate_60s >= 0.65) && (prefill_est_ms <= 0.4 * slo_ms). Candidate tweak: kv_threshold=0.8 and prefill_budget_frac=0.4. Added 300ms hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.

maya: Note higher kv threshold lowers hit-rate and ups compute cost. Did you run a cost delta?

perf-bot: quick cost summary: model C token_cost_kv_hit=0.007 credits/token, miss=0.028 credits/token. observed kv_hit drop 0.76->0.63 in canary => approx +20% token compute cost at peak. But p95 improved ~18% which reduces SLA exposure for high-tier tenants.

jess: This should be tenant-scoped. prod-sla tenants can accept cost increase; defaults maybe keep looser gate.

sam: proposal for per-tenant defaults:
- prod-sla: prefill_budget_frac=0.35, kv_thresh=0.85, microbatch_target=6
- default: prefill_budget_frac=0.5, kv_thresh=0.65, microbatch_target=8

ian: Runtime impl note: evaluating kv gate per request is expensive. Suggest a compact bitfield state per pool (slot_admit_state) updated every 200-300ms and read atomically by scheduler. Keeps fast path cheap.

sam: added config snippet in branch: 
```
latency_budget_gate:
  prefill_fraction: 0.4
  kv_admit_threshold: 0.8
  microbatch_target: 6
  hysteresis_ms: 300
```

maya: Can you run a 30m soak with 3x tail spike injection and capture kernel-fallback histogram + cpu/mem? Prefer canary pool.

sam: will run today: plan canary 10% -> 30% -> 60% across 48h if soak looks stable. Will post tables.

jess: Add an A/B: half of canary gets kernel pinning (sticky kernel selection during request) to measure fallback overhead. If pinning + mb=6 reduces p99 further, we consider making kernel selection sticky when warm.

ian: Also consider gating prefill budget by kv_warm_rate (fraction of newly populated entries per minute). If kv_warm_rate < 0.08 bias to larger prefill to warm cache.

sam: good idea; will add kv_warm_rate gating. Action items:
- sam: 30m soak + kernel-fallback histogram + p95/p99 (today)
- jess: set up A/B kernel pinning configs (this afternoon)
- ian: implement slot_admit_state fast path (PR by EOD tomorrow)
- maya: run cost impact by tenant tier and update playbook (tomorrow)

sam: TL;DR: microbatch=6 + latency-budget kv gate improves p95/p99 with manageable cost for SLA tenants. Need per-tenant tuning, short hysteresis, and kernel pinning A/B to validate.

maya: :thumbsup: any infra blockers?

ian: none, just watch host CPU when kv-hit drops; will add temporary alert for cpu/token spikes.
